manual_review.rule: Protocol v0.10 §18.1. Each hit or exposure is a lead for a manual reading (controlled.audit_fresh_attempt_transcript), and every flagged access was read in its transcript. An attempt that read, listed or searched anything outside its workspace fails and is excluded; an attempt that only read or listed its own workspace, or touched only system locations (interpreters, system libraries, the container's temporary directory /tmp), passes. A harness notice naming a file the attempt never opened, a token the parser resolved against the wrong directory, and a call the permission system denied before it ran do not exclude an attempt. The build session's scratch directory is not a system location: it is a Claude session directory that holds the build session's working records, and §15.4, §16.2 and the fresh-attempt profile count it as forbidden.
manual_review.note: judged_false_positive lists the flagged attempts whose flags, on reading, mark no read, listing or search of material outside the workspace; false_positive_kinds says why. 'excluded' above is the script's own list of flagged attempts. After the reading, the attempts excluded from every analysis are those in excluded_after_review; each candidate's attempt record carries the verdict (audit.passed). The sensitivity analysis of §18.1 excludes every attempt in flagged_by_script instead.
manual_review.independent_sweep: Beyond the flagged accesses, every tool call of the 20 transcripts was read for this review: the paths of the file tools, each shell command's working directory and the absolute and relative paths it names, every listing and recursive search, the host programs it ran, every tool other than the file tools, the shell and the final hand-back, and the tool outputs for paths outside the workspace. No file tool named a path outside its workspace, and no Grep or Glob ran without a path. 322 of the 328 shell commands began with a cd into the workspace; the other 6 named only absolute paths (in the workspace, in /tmp, or, in CS-02-fresh-A-final-1, in the build session's scratch directory) before any cd into the workspace. Every listing and recursive search stayed inside the workspace, and every relative parent reference resolved inside it. Besides the shell's standard utilities, the host programs run were git, on the workspace's own repository, the system python3, and the workspace's wrappers, through which alone the repository's code ran. The only accesses outside a workspace were CS-02-fresh-A-final-1's use of the build session's scratch directory (excluded), files of their own in /tmp, the container's temporary directory (CS-02-fresh-B-u1-5, CS-02-fresh-B-final-1, CS-02-fresh-B-final-2), and one call naming a file under /root that the permission classifier denied before it ran (CS-02-fresh-B-u1-3). One attempt (CS-02-fresh-B-u1-5) called TaskStop once, on its own background command. The wrappers and the instruction file of every workspace are unchanged.
manual_review.outside_scope: Harness context that is not a tool input or output was not scanned by the script: every attempt was given the build session's environment details (its working directory, the study repository, and its scratch path, named there as the place for temporary files), and all 20 received reminders listing the build session's task titles (61 in all). Read for this review, they hold no reference, transcript, verifier, candidate or label of CS-02; no attempt used a task tool on them or opened a path they name, except that CS-02-fresh-A-final-1 wrote its helper files into the scratch path (see its review).
